experiments.description: Simulation study of the proposed quantum interior-point method for constrained portfolio optimization on real market data, using the cvxportfolio S&P-500 dataset and varying problem sizes to estimate condition number, tomography precision, and empirical runtime scaling.

algorithm.variant: Quantum short-step interior-point method for SOCP-based constrained portfolio optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Run for T = O(sqrt(r) log(n/epsilon)) iterations until target precision epsilon is reached; experiments use fixed epsilon = 0.1 in the scalability study

hyperparameters.problem_sizes: random subsets with 100 companies and random time windows t uniform in [10, 500]

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Historical returns are used to compute mu and M; M is stored in QRAM and used to build the SOCP constraint matrix and Newton matrices. Portfolio variables are represented in the SOCP with Lorentz-cone variables and positivity constraints.
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize x^T Sigma x subject to mu^T x = R and x >= 0, with Sigma = M^T M
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraints are enforced through SOCP reformulation; positivity constraints via Lorentz cones L_0, equality constraints via linear constraints in the SOCP

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization instances derived from the cvxportfolio repository; S&P-500 stock data over 2007-2016, subsampled for experiments.

dataset_specification.description: Historical data for S&P-500 companies over 9 years (2007-2016); experiments use a subsample of 50 companies and the first 100 days for the main simulation study; scalability study uses random subsets of 100 companies and random subintervals of length t with t uniform in [10, 500].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute mean returns mu and matrix M from historical returns; covariance is represented as Sigma = M^T M; no additional preprocessing reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulate the quantum algorithm by adding Gaussian noise corresponding to tomography precision; compare against noiseless classical simulation; record duality gap, tomography precision, condition number, and estimated complexity across iterations and across random problem sizes.

noise_model.noise_type: Gaussian noise added to emulate tomography precision

noise_parameters.noise_magnitude: corresponding to tomography precision in Theorem 6.5

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical short-step interior-point method / SOCP solver baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute mu and M from historical returns; build SOCP formulation and constraint matrices.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recover portfolio x from the SOCP solution; for the simulation study, compare duality gap and condition number trajectories and fit power laws to observed scaling.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: duality gap decreases multiplicatively; tomography precision also decreases after a point

classical_baselines.method_name: classical short-step interior-point method / SOCP solver baseline
classical_baselines.unit: O(n^3.5) in practice; more generally O~(n^(omega+0.5) log(1/epsilon))

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup; potentially O(n) speedup in practice
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical short-step interior-point method / SOCP solver
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming bounded problem-dependent parameters kappa and zeta, and moderate tomography precision delta; for large n and small r
speedup_claims.caveats: Quantum runtime depends on kappa, zeta, and 1/delta^2; speedup is not worst-case guaranteed. The paper also notes the practical classical complexity is about O(n^3.5), while the quantum estimate from experiments is about O(n^2.387), implying an almost O(n) speedup for most instances.

speedup_claims.conditions: based on fitted average-case complexity over sampled instances with epsilon = 0.1
speedup_claims.caveats: Derived from power-law fit to estimated complexity, not from wall-clock quantum hardware execution.

speedup_claims.factor: O~(n^1.5 zeta kappa / delta^2 log(1/epsilon)) vs O~(n^(omega+0.5) log(1/epsilon))
speedup_claims.conditions: well-conditioned Newton systems and efficient QRAM/block-encoding access
